name: ICES DOME: contaminants and effects in biota, sediment and seawater
custodian: International Council for the Exploration of the Sea
measures: Pb, Hg, Cd and other contaminants in marine sediment, seawater and biota, from the OSPAR CEMP and HELCOM COMBINE monitoring programmes
why_it_matters: The measured European range that this demonstrator's hypothetical hotspot should be compared against. The default porewater Pb of 1.0 mg/L is far above typical values and this is the dataset that shows it.
format: CSV download after accepting the ICES data policy; download and functional web services available
licence: CC BY 4.0 for all public data
notes: Not redistributed here. Sediment concentrations are not porewater concentrations, and the model needs porewater; converting between them requires a partition coefficient that is itself a fitted quantity.

name: Data and results for the 2024 OSPAR CEMP assessment
measures: assessed levels and trends of hazardous substances including Hg, Cd and Pb in sediment and biota
why_it_matters: Quality-controlled assessment output, so it can be cited without re-deriving the statistics.
notes: The OSPAR Hazardous Substances Assessment Tool at https://dome.ices.dk/ohat/ exposes the same assessment interactively.

name: OSPAR ODIMS datastreams
measures: OSPAR data and information streams, including hazardous substances
why_it_matters: The route to OSPAR's own holdings rather than a summary of them.

name: EMODnet Chemistry contaminant products
custodian: European Marine Observation and Data Network
measures: aggregated and validated concentrations of 12 MSFD-prioritised pollutants including lead and mercury, in seawater, sediment and biota
why_it_matters: The European counterpart to D1, with mapped spatial coverage. Useful for saying what a realistic European site looks like without naming one.
format: map viewer plus product catalogue downloads
notes: Method paper: Frontiers in Marine Science 7:583657, DOI 10.3389/fmars.2020.583657.

name: HELCOM metals core indicator (lead, cadmium, mercury)
measures: status and trends for Pb, Cd and Hg in water, biota and sediment
why_it_matters: Baltic context, which is where marine munitions contamination is most documented, without asserting a hotspot at any location.
format: indicator reports plus the HELCOM Map and Data Service

name: In situ measured benthic fluxes of dissolved inorganic phosphorus in the Baltic Sea
custodian: Hylen, A. et al., via Zenodo
measures: 498 in-situ fluxes from three types of benthic chamber lander at 59 stations over 20 years, with bottom-water oxygen, sediment organic carbon and sediment type
why_it_matters: A method and data-structure reference for benthic chamber measurement, which is the acquisition kind the demonstrator's flux observations imitate.
notes: PHOSPHORUS ONLY. It contains no trace metal fluxes and must not be cited as a metals source.

name: Use of Amendments for In Situ Remediation at Superfund Sediment Sites
measures: regulatory and performance record for activated-carbon amendment and reactive capping
why_it_matters: Establishes that reactive capping is deployed practice, which is why this project claims no novelty for it.

name: Development of a benthic-flux chamber, USGS SIR 2004-5298
measures: benthic flux chamber design and measurement chain
why_it_matters: Documents what a chamber does and does not measure, which is the basis for refusing to treat a chamber result as a whole-footprint annual flux.

name: Measured Pb or Hg flux attenuation across a marine reactive cap
why_it_matters: No open dataset of this was found. The closest evidence is organic-contaminant flux attenuation in a Norwegian harbour field trial (E1) and a metals mesocosm (E3). The absence is itself a finding: the headline quantity of this concept has not been measured in the open literature for metals in a marine cap.
notes: Searched: benthic flux chamber metal flux capping, reactive cap flux attenuation metals, EMODnet and ICES holdings, Zenodo and Mendeley Data.

name: Keratin biosorption isotherms in seawater
measures: Pb and Hg uptake on a keratin biosorbent at seawater pH and ionic strength
why_it_matters: Every published keratin capacity found is deionised water at acidic pH. No seawater isotherm was found, and no verified keratin Hg capacity of any kind was found. This is the largest single uncertainty in the model.
notes: Searched: Zenodo, Mendeley Data, CORE, AGRIS, and the keratin biosorption review literature. See docs/MATERIAL_KERATIN.md section 3.
